question: The Greek fruit processing industry is highly export-oriented, with 98 % of fruit compote production exported. This vital sector of the Greek economy is constantly challenged by actions by countries such as the US and China. The US reintroduced tariffs on steel and aluminium imports from the EU, on the basis of Section 232 of its Trade Expansion Act, on the grounds of ‘national security’.

It is also considering extending these tariffs to related products, such as canned foods. This would see Greek compote exports subject to duties of up to 50 % on the value of the metal container, thus increasing costs and reducing the product’s competitiveness. At the same time, cheap Chinese compote exports to the EU are increasing rapidly, rising by 44 % in the three-year period from 2020 to 2023.

Its prices, 20-30 % lower than the costs of Greek producers, are the result of a strategy of unfair pricing (dumping), supported by state subsidies and low energy and labour costs. This combined framework creates artificially low prices, allowing Chinese producers to increase their foothold in the European compote market to the detriment of European producers. Can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What initiatives will it take to ensure that any additional US tariffs are not extended to imports of canned food, which would affect the cost and competitiveness of products such as fruit compote?
Does it intend to immediately activate the available anti-dumping tools to protect European fruit compote producers from unfair competition from China?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.12.2025) The Commission is closely monitoring developments concerning the possible extension of United States Section 232 measures to canned food products. The Commission maintains regular communication with the United States authorities at both technical and political levels to ensure that the EU’s interests are fully taken into account.

In this context, the Commission is requesting that the United States exempt EU exports from any further extension of Section 232 measures on steel and aluminium derivatives. This would preserve the spirit of the political deal agreed by the President of the Commission and the President of the United States, as reflected in the Joint Statement1.

This would ensure that EU exports of canned goods and fruit compotes are only subject to the single, all-inclusive 15% tariff rate, and do not face any other duties or further administrative requirements. The Commission will continue to advocate for EU consumers, producers and exporters. The Commission is fully committed to protecting EU industries from unfair competition from imports.

The EU has over 220 trade defence measures in place, including – since 2008 – antidumping measures on imports of prepared or preserved citrus fruits from China2, under expiry review since 21 October 2025. The Commission conducts investigations where it receives evidence from any affected EU industry of injury suffered from dumped and/or subsidised imports and that action is warranted.
The peach compote industry is invited to contact the Commission’s trade defence services3 to discuss the issues of concern.
